title: SIRTUINS: POTENTIAL PHARMACOLOGICAL TARGET IN VARIOUS DISORDERS
venue: International Journal of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
abstract: Sirtuins are a group of NAD+-dependent protein deacetylases that play an important role in cellular homeostasis, with wide-ranging effects on health and disease. Gene expression, metabolism, DNA repair, stress responses, and longevity are just a few of the biological processes that are affected by these evolutionarily conserved enzymes. Seven sirtuin subtypes (SIRT1–SIRT7) comprise the sirtuin family, and each has unique enzymatic properties and subcellular locations. Sirtuins are essential agents in chromatin remodelling, coordinating epigenetic changes that affect gene transcription and cellular destiny. Additionally, they play a crucial role in controlling pathways for nutrition sensing and energy homeostasis, which regulate the cellular metabolism. Notably, sirtuins participate in DNA repair and affect cell cycle progression, both of which are essential for maintaining genomic stability. This article offers a thorough overview of sirtuin biology, with an emphasis on their numerous roles, cellular localization, and consequences in various physiological and pathological circumstances.
